requirements.requirement: Apply the security updates available from node1's configured software repositories.
requirements.summary: The enabled CentOS Stream repositories initially offered numerous package updates but exposed no security-advisory metadata. A full repository upgrade completed successfully, updated security-sensitive packages and installed the newer kernel, and package checks both before and after reboot found no remaining repository updates.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the existing inventory data while applying the updates.
requirements.summary: The final and post-reboot SHA-256 hashes exactly match the preparation baseline for both inventory files. Contents remain valid, and ownership, modes, and sizes were preserved.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged the restart, returned with a different boot ID and the updated kernel, and recovered its services, package health, network presence, and unchanged inventory. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: The repositories supplied no updateinfo/security-advisory metadata, so the evidence cannot map installed versions to named security advisories or CVEs; the successful full upgrade and zero remaining updates nevertheless show that every available package update was applied.
Final presence or cleanup of the two monitoring files under /var/tmp was not directly observed.
No cluster-state probe was applicable because the managed topology contains only the standalone node1.
Requirement preserve-inventory-data cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-inventory-data

operational_hygiene.summary: No unrelated unnecessary mutation was established. Repository-cache refresh was relevant discovery, the full upgrade was a reasonable fallback given the missing advisory metadata, and the reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. The recovered node had healthy package state, no failed services, and the same effective listener set. One minor caveat is that the upgrade command created /var/tmp/security-upgrade.log and /var/tmp/security-upgrade.pid for bounded monitoring; no cleanup is shown and the lifecycle snapshots did not inspect /var/tmp, so whether this possible residue remained is indeterminate. Expected reboot-generated systemd private directories were not penalized.
